title: Python packaging: dev and ai extras, correct build floor, Trusted Publishing
description:
Problem: 'pip install kanbus' resolves to 96 packages and 381 MB, of which the core runtime (click, pydantic, pyyaml, jinja2, requests, paho-mqtt, markus, virtuus, pydantic-settings) is 23 packages and 21 MB. litellm alone adds 37 packages and 248 MB and is already lazily imported (right_now.py:875, summarize.py:29); dev tools (behave, pytest, gherkin-official, coverage, ruff, black, sphinx) add 30 packages and 109 MB and pin formatter versions on users (python/pyproject.toml:12-30; already filed as kbs-abc0e83f, this task is the implementation). pyproject.toml:2 requires setuptools>=68 but line 10 uses the PEP 639 license = 'MIT' field, which fails prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel on setuptools 75 (needs 77). CI tests Python 3.11 only while classifiers claim 3.12 and 3.13. A stale 'kanbusr' entry point remains (pyproject.toml:48-50). release.yml publishes with long-lived PYPI_TOKEN and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. The published wheel lacks the license file.

Work: move dev tools to [project.optional-dependencies] dev (install -e python[dev] in CI); make litellm an 'ai' extra with a clear error when the AI commands run without it; requires = ['setuptools>=77'] and license-files; drop kanbusr; a small 3.11/3.12/3.13 matrix for the unit-test job; PyPI and crates.io Trusted Publishing where the registries allow it.

Acceptance: a fresh 'pip install kanbus' from the built wheel installs under 30 packages; 'kanbus --help' still under 0.5 s; python -m build succeeds with setuptools 77 in an isolated env; wheel contains LICENSE.
